page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan. Left page: running head at top with page number at top left; one column of running text with a left margin note beside the line "bis injuriam facit"; no text below the main text. Right page: cropped at the gutter, showing only the word-ends of its lines at the right edge; no legible text.

tem : quin ut iplis liceat, pro arbitratu suo, &
tur expedire, eandem apud subditos suos fancire,
XXXI. Dico Quarto, Legem Moralem, à Mose
traditam, hoc est, Præcepta Decalogi, obligare om-
nes Christianos, pariter ac Judæos, ad eam obser-
vandam. Et hoc quidem omnes, quod sciam,
Protestantes uno ore confitentur : quod majorem no-
bis injuriam facit Bellarminus, qui nos fingit in
eponere Christianam libertatem, ut nulli legi sub-
jecti simus in Conscientia, Mofes autem cum suo
Decalogo nihil ad nos pertineat. Viderit quomodo
se calumnia liberet ; suofque (si nos in hac culpa)
eodem crimine. Agitatur enim haec con-
troversia inter suos Scholasticos, teneanturne Chri-
stiani Præceptis Decalogi, quatenus sunt decla-
rativa Legis Naturæ tantum, an etiam quatenus sunt
Mosi à Deo, Deíque jussu à Mose populo Dei tr-
adita, & in sacros Codices relata : aliis utrumque
affirmantibus, aliis è duobus alterum negantibus.
Est & in nostris Ecclesiis eandem reperire hac de
illi inter se, & nos cum illis in eo quod rei caput
legem earn, quæ à Mose tradita est in præcepti
Decalogi continetur, vim obligandi nostras Chri-
stianorum conscientias : fortasse non est operæ
pretium, unde illam obligandi vim obtineat, mul-
tum litigare. Consultius tamen mihi loqui vide-
tur qui dicunt Legem illam Mosis non obligare
Christianos formaliter & qua talis, hoc est qua-
tenus à Mose tradita est ; sed tantum ratione

page.notes: The right page is cut off at the gutter; only word-ends are visible, so its lines are given as fragments marked [?] and not as full words. The final word of the left page is split across two lines ("au-" / "thoritate"); the completion is doubtful. The page number "o3" is printed in old-style figures and is read as 63 with [?]. The marginal note "5." beside "ponere" is read as part of the note "Bellarm. 4. de Justific. 5.", and "in e" at the line end is cut off by the scan edge, so it is marked as the likely start of "in ea". Long s is written as plain s in the running head and text.
